notes: limits.py holds a LIMITS dict of (threshold, window) tuples per scope; the threshold is read only by limits.exhausted, so M1 and M5 change the first element of the SIGN_IN and DEMO tuples and leave the windows and the overall DEMO_ALL limit alone. views.sign_in locks the address's counter (an upsert) inside one transaction, asks exhausted(), then validates, authenticates and either starts the session or records a failure: M2 authenticates first and refuses only a failure at the limit, and M4 zeroes the locked counter with save(update_fields) on success, inside the transaction, before the session is cycled (record() then treats the zero count as a new window). M3 reads the first X-Forwarded-For entry, falling back to REMOTE_ADDR, in limits.client_key, the one client-address function both per-address limits use.
